content.title: What is IoT (Internet of Things)? | Microsoft Azure
content.text: IoT use cases and examples The Internet of Things provides real-time visibility, automation, and big data analytics capabilities that help any organization—regardless of size or industry—gain a competitive advantage. Plus, IoT devices also empower consumers to improve their day to day by making key functions more convenient. Industrial IoT IoT transforms industrial environments—like manufacturing plants, energy operations, and logistics networks—by equipping machines, equipment, and infrastructure with connected sensors that give organizations real-time insights into operational performance. Plus, they empower teams to automate tedious or time-consuming tasks that previously required manual intervention. Common industrial IoT use cases include: Predictive maintenance. Detect early signs of equipment failure to help minimize unplanned downtime.Remote asset monitoring. Get realtime visibility into machinery, fleets, or environmental conditions across locations.Factory automation. Streamline workflows and automatically regulate product quality using IoT devices that autonomously collect and act on data.Energy management. Track and optimize energy consumption to lower costs and reduce your carbon footprint.Industrial safety and compliance. Proactively detect hazards, monitor worker conditions, and trigger automated safety protocols to ensure compliance with regulatory standards. Healthcare IoT IoT devices reshape clinical workflows, patient experiences, and medical outcomes by significantly increasing visibility into patient health and streamlining operations. Using IoT devices, care teams can adopt proactive strategies and deliver higher quality care more efficiently. Common healthcare IoT use cases include: Remote patient care. Continuously monitor and track vitals like heart rate, blood pressure, and glucose levels to proactively address patient needs.Equipment management. Monitor usage and track device location in real time to improve equipment allocation and reduce downtime.Smart hospital infrastructure. Maintain patient comfort by automatically detecting and adjusting to changes in temperature, air quality, and humidity.Inhome care and support. Offer wearables and other IoT-enabled devices that detect falls or abnormal patterns to help teams assist aging populations and chroniccare patients. Consumer IoT In addition to helping organizations gain a competitive edge, IoT brings connected intelligence into everyday life, enabling seamless control, personalization, and automation across homes, vehicles, and personal devices. By linking sensors, apps, and cloud services, consumer IoT helps individuals gain greater convenience, safety, and realtime insights while simplifying routine tasks and everyday functions. Common consumer IoT use cases include: Smart homes. Automatically heat and cool your home and adjust lighting while reducing energy costs.Wearables and fitness trackers. Monitor aspects of your health in real time, including your activity, sleep, and biometric patterns.Home security and safety. Detect and automatically react to motion or camera detection by sending alerts or locking doors.Smart vehicles. Get real-time car diagnostics to help troubleshoot issues and navigation insights to personalize your driving experience.
